public_payload.normalized_proposition: Fully autonomous Level 5 driverless cars that safely go from any point A to any point B will not arrive any time soon.

statement.excerpt: More than that we just shouldn’t expect fully autonomous (Level 5) driverless cars—safely taking us from any old point A to any old point B—any time soon.
statement.document_title: Will Tesla ever “Solve” Full Self Driving?

from_speaker: safely taking us from any old point A to any old point B
our_interpretation: The target is unrestricted Level 5 driving under conditions a competent human driver could handle. Geographically restricted driverless services do not meet that threshold.
Arrival means demonstrated deployment for passenger transport, rather than an announcement or a selected demonstration.
Any time soon expresses a near-term forecast but supplies no determinate deadline. October 2026 is the evaluation cutoff, not a deadline Marcus supplied.
Safely does not mean that a vehicle must be incapable of ever having an accident.
criteria.support_condition: Reliable deployment records show that qualifying Level 5 vehicles did not arrive throughout the intended near-term period. A final supportive judgment requires a defensible endpoint for that period.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Independent evidence establishes deployment of safe, unrestricted Level 5 passenger vehicles sufficiently close to publication to fall clearly within the ordinary meaning of any time soon.
